items.label: f01-presigned-url
items.front: What is SigV4 presigning, and what can the holder of a presigned URL do?
items.back: The server computes a signature over the one request it wants to authorise and embeds it in the query string (X-Amz-Signature, -Credential, -Date, -Expires). The holder can make that one request until expiresIn elapses, and nothing else; the secret key never leaves the server.

items.label: f03-v1-v2-exercise
items.front: Why are elihyper2's v2 unit tests (cd app && npm test) runnable without AWS credentials, and what does that tell you?
items.back: v2 builds the Express app with injected AWS clients, so tests (plain node --test) pass fake Polly/Claude stand-ins (createFakePolly, createFakeClaude) and assert e.g. GET /health never touches AWS. The AWS calls live behind injected dependencies at the edge, not inside the logic under test.

items.label: f02-cors-budget-drain
items.front: nova-bpt v1 issue 6.2: app.use(cors()) on credential-backed endpoints. Why is it high severity before any deployment?
items.back: cors() with no options allows any origin, and /get-signed-url hands out direct AWS access with no auth and no rate limit, so one link click on any site can drain the AWS budget. STORY-04 locks down CORS and adds rate limiting.

items.prompt: In nova-bpt v1, how does the trust pattern of /get-signed-url differ from /speak and /ask-claude?

choices.text: It is a proxy too, relaying every audio chunk through the server process
It is the only endpoint that requires an authenticated, signed-in user
A credential broker: the server signs a URL and the browser goes to AWS
It hands the AWS secret key itself to the browser for five minutes

choices: It is a proxy too, relaying every audio chunk through the server process
It is the only endpoint that requires an authenticated, signed-in user
A credential broker: the server signs a URL and the browser goes to AWS
It hands the AWS secret key itself to the browser for five minutes

items.explanation: '/speak and /ask-claude are a proxy... /get-signed-url is a credential broker. The server signs a URL and hands it over; the browser then talks to AWS directly over a WebSocket.'

items.prompt: v1 uses express.static('public'). You start the server from the parent directory. What happens to the HTML pages?

choices.text: Express falls back to serving the files from node_modules instead
They 404, because the path resolves against the cwd, not server.js
The server refuses to start, because the public folder is missing
They load normally, since Express resolves paths relative to the entry file

choices: Express falls back to serving the files from node_modules instead
They 404, because the path resolves against the cwd, not server.js
The server refuses to start, because the public folder is missing
They load normally, since Express resolves paths relative to the entry file

items.explanation: 'express.static('public') resolves relative to the process working directory, not to server.js... Prefer express.static(path.join(__dirname, 'public')).'

items.prompt: In an AWS event-stream audio frame, which part is little-endian?

choices.text: Only the two CRC32 checksums at the prelude and at the end
Everything, because Web Audio produces little-endian Float32 data
Only the PCM samples in the payload; the framing is big-endian
Only the total-length and headers-length prelude fields

choices: Only the two CRC32 checksums at the prelude and at the end
Everything, because Web Audio produces little-endian Float32 data
Only the PCM samples in the payload; the framing is big-endian
Only the total-length and headers-length prelude fields

items.explanation: 'Everything here is big-endian except the PCM samples inside the payload, which are little-endian. Mixing those up is the classic bug in this code path.'

items.prompt: What does hoisting new PollyClient(...) out of the /speak handler to module scope buy?

choices.text: Reuse of the client, credential resolver and connections across requests
It lets Polly accept more than 3000 characters in a single call
It is required for AudioStream.pipe(res) to stream the audio back
It makes the voice and engine configurable on each request

choices: Reuse of the client, credential resolver and connections across requests
It lets Polly accept more than 3000 characters in a single call
It is required for AudioStream.pipe(res) to stream the audio back
It makes the voice and engine configurable on each request

items.explanation: The in-handler client 'builds a fresh client, credential resolver and HTTP agent on every request. Hoisting it to module scope is a one-line change and lets the SDK reuse connections.'

items.prompt: The presigner is configured with service: "transcribestreaming" to match the hostname. What is the symptom?

choices.text: An opaque 403 on WebSocket connect; the signing name must be transcribe
The URL expires immediately instead of lasting the full five minutes
Nothing at all: SigV4 accepts either service name for Transcribe streaming
A DNS failure, because the hostname is rebuilt from the signing service name

choices: An opaque 403 on WebSocket connect; the signing name must be transcribe
The URL expires immediately instead of lasting the full five minutes
Nothing at all: SigV4 accepts either service name for Transcribe streaming
A DNS failure, because the hostname is rebuilt from the signing service name

items.explanation: 'service: "transcribe" — not "transcribestreaming". The signing service name and the hostname prefix differ. Getting this wrong produces an opaque 403 on WebSocket connect.'

items.prompt: In v1, a user types 'what is 2+2' into claude.html. Why do they see 'Error.'?

choices.text: The Claude model ID had expired, so Bedrock returned a 404 for the call
Bedrock rejects any prompt shorter than ten characters with a 400 error
CORS blocks the request, because claude.html sets no Origin header
server.js JSON.parses the raw prompt string, which throws into a 500

choices: The Claude model ID had expired, so Bedrock returned a 404 for the call
Bedrock rejects any prompt shorter than ten characters with a 400 error
CORS blocks the request, because claude.html sets no Origin header
server.js JSON.parses the raw prompt string, which throws into a 500

items.explanation: claude.html sends { prompt: input } as a raw string; server.js does JSON.parse(req.body.prompt), which throws for 'what is 2+2'; the catch returns 500 and the page renders 'Error.'. A contract regression from commit f8dba37.

items.prompt: Why are the x-amzn-transcribe-* headers excluded from the SigV4 presign signature?

choices.text: They carry the secret access key, which must never be part of a signature
AWS forbids signing any header whose name starts with the x-amzn prefix
Excluding them keeps the URL shorter than the browser's length limit
Browser WebSockets can't send custom headers, so signing them never matches

choices: They carry the secret access key, which must never be part of a signature
AWS forbids signing any header whose name starts with the x-amzn prefix
Excluding them keeps the URL shorter than the browser's length limit
Browser WebSockets can't send custom headers, so signing them never matches

items.explanation: 'a browser WebSocket cannot send custom headers. If they were signed, the signature would never match what the browser actually sends.' Query parameters do the real work.

items.prompt: A Transcribe result arrives with IsPartial: true. How should the page treat it?

choices.text: As final text, since Transcribe only ever sends confident results
As an error frame that should close the WebSocket immediately
As a duplicate of the previous final result, to be discarded
As a running guess to replace, not append to the final transcript

choices: As final text, since Transcribe only ever sends confident results
As an error frame that should close the WebSocket immediately
As a duplicate of the previous final result, to be discarded
As a running guess to replace, not append to the final transcript

items.explanation: 'IsPartial: true means "this will change"... IsPartial: false means "this is settled" — the code appends it to the output.'

items.prompt: Why does v1 broker a signed URL for Transcribe instead of proxying the stream, and what is the cost?

choices.text: Transcribe rejects server IPs; the cost is that captions arrive out of order
Browsers cannot open WebSockets to localhost; the cost is an extra TLS handshake
Signed URLs are cheaper on AWS billing; the cost is losing all partial results
Proxying means relaying every chunk; the cost is 5 min of unmetered AWS access

choices: Transcribe rejects server IPs; the cost is that captions arrive out of order
Browsers cannot open WebSockets to localhost; the cost is an extra TLS handshake
Signed URLs are cheaper on AWS billing; the cost is losing all partial results
Proxying means relaying every chunk; the cost is 5 min of unmetered AWS access

items.explanation: Transcribe streaming is long-lived and bidirectional; brokering is simpler and lower latency. 'The tradeoff is that anyone who can reach /get-signed-url gets five minutes of direct, unmetered access.' Anyone who can reach the endpoint gets that access.

items.prompt: Why is an async onaudioprocess handler that awaits resampling before socket.send() dangerous?

choices.text: Callbacks don't wait, so two in flight can send audio out of order
Resampling asynchronously flips the endianness of the PCM samples
Awaiting inside the handler blocks the WebSocket from receiving events
The handler runs only once, because async callbacks are not re-entrant

choices: Callbacks don't wait, so two in flight can send audio out of order
Resampling asynchronously flips the endianness of the PCM samples
Awaiting inside the handler blocks the WebSocket from receiving events
The handler runs only once, because async callbacks are not re-entrant

items.explanation: 'onaudioprocess fires on a fixed cadence and does not wait for the previous promise. If two callbacks are ever in flight, their socket.send() calls can land out of order.' Rare, and 'rarely is the worst kind of bug.'

items.prompt: The v1 /ask-claude handler returns responseBody.content[0].text. What assumption is that line making?

choices.text: That the first content block is a text block
That content is a string rather than an array of blocks
That the anthropic_version field names the model version
That the model always returns exactly one output token

choices: That the first content block is a text block
That content is a string rather than an array of blocks
That the anthropic_version field names the model version
That the model always returns exactly one output token

items.explanation: 'responseBody.content is an array of content blocks, and the code assumes content[0] is a text block. That is true for a plain text reply, but it is a load-bearing assumption.' That holds for a plain reply, but it is load-bearing.
